To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presented ΣΔ modulator is designed for closing the loop of a digital audio amplifier, that the modulator is a continuous-time third order ΣΔ modulator, that it is designed in 40nm CMOS technology, that it consumes 1.1V, that it achieves 101dB DR, and that it achieves 72dB peak SNDR.

the presented continuous-time third-order $\Sigma\Delta $ modulator is designed for closing the loop of a digital closed-loop class-D audio amplifier, and that the proposed modulator achieves a dynamic-range of 101dB, a peak signal-to-noiseratio (SNDR) of 72dB, and a power consumption of 1.7mW from a 5V power supply.
we have demonstrated a continuous-time ΣΔ ADC with a 1.7mW power consumption, which is suitable to be used in a digital closed-loop class-D audio amplifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high performance, low power, and low voltage continuous-time ΣΔ modulator for digital class-D audio amplifiers.
the implementation of an efficient, low-power, and high-performance ΣΔ modulator for the digital closed-loop class-D audio amplifier.
the design of an efficient and flexible class-D power amplifier (PAM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed ΣΔ modulators are a very good solution to achieve the best performance in terms of dynamic-range (101 dB) and power consumption (1.7 m W) in a 40 nm CMOS technology.
the paper presents a very good design of a ΣΔ modulator for the specific application of a digital class D amplifier.

the proposed 1.1V, 40 nm CMOS, 101 dB DR, 1.8 mW continuous-time Sigma-Delta ADC for a digital closed-loop class-D amplifier is the first of its kind and a very important milestone in the field of digital audio amplification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented ΣΔ ADC achieves the best performance in the literature for the considered technology and supply voltage.
we have developed a new class-D audio amplifier architecture that is fully implemented in digital domain, which is the most flexible and programmable solution for the future of audio amplifiers.
we designed a 101 dB dynamic range, 1.6 mW power consumption, 1.5 V supply, 1.2 MHz sampling frequency continuous time sigma delta ADC in a 0.4 micron CMOS technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed ΣΔ modulators can be used in a wide range of applications, from low-power portable devices to professional audio equipment.
the ΣΔ modulator can be designed with the same specifications as the class-D amplifier.

, in contrast to the conventional wisdom that the ΣΔ ADC must be designed for the application, we show that a ΣΔ modulator can be designed first, and then its outputs can be used in a variety of applications, including the one considered in this paper.
